questions.question: The selling price of x items is equal to the cost price of 32 items and profit percent is 28%. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

SP of x items = CP of 32 items

Profit % = 28

**Concept used:**

SP = CP + CP × profit%

SP = selling price

CP = cost price

**Calculation:**

Let CP of each item be Rs. 100a

So, CP of x item = Rs. 100xa

SP of each item = 128xa

According to the question,

x.SP = 32.CP

⇒ 128ax = 3200a

⇒ x = 3200a/128a

⇒ x = 25

So, x = 25 items

**∴ The value of x is 25.**

questions.question: Price ceiling refers to:

options.text: removal of tax from already costly goods or services
imposition of tax on all the prices of goods or services
imposition of lower limit of tax on costly goods or services
imposition of upper limit of price on goods or services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**imposition of upper limit of price on goods or services.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A** price ceiling** is a sort of **price regulation** that establishes the **maximum price **a seller may charge for a good or service and is typically imposed by the **government.**
 
• These are often imposed on necessities like **food, gas, or medicine**, frequently following a **crisis or specific occurrence** that causes prices to soar.
 
• The** benefits** of a price floor include maintaining **affordable pricing, preventing price gouging, and growing demands.**
 
• Price floor **disadvantages **include** frequent supply shortages, the potential for quality loss and cost-cutting**, as well as the possibility of** additional fees or higher costs** for other commodities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Price Floor:**

 
 
• A price floor, which establishes a **minimum cost for purchasing** a good or service, is the opposite of a price ceiling.
 
• It stands for the** lowest legal price** at which a good or service may be offered and still adhere to the basic laws of supply and demand.
 
• This is also known as "**price support."**
 
 
 
• **GST:**
 
 
• An** indirect tax **on the provision of goods and services is known as the GST, or **Goods and Services Tax. **
 
• It is a **multi-stage, destination-oriented tax** imposed on every value addition, replacing multiple indirect taxes, including VAT, excise duty, service taxes, etc

questions.question: The inputs used in the production of goods or services to make an economic profit are known as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**factors of production.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **inputs** utilized in the** creation of goods or services **to generate a profit are referred to as** factors of production.**
 
• These include all materials required for producing a good or service.
 
• **Land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship** are the production factors.
 
• The overall factors of production can be impacted by the** status of technical development,** which can also account for any **efficiencies **not directly related to the four traditional components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Four factors of production**—land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship.
 
• **Land:**
 
 
• Every **natural resource utilized** to produce goods and services is included in land.
 
• **Water, oil, copper, natural gas, coal, and forests** are a few examples.
 
• The** raw materials used in the industrial process **are land resources. These resources can be both **renewable and nonrenewable.**
 
 
 
• **Labor:**
 
 
• The** effort that people put forth** to produce goods and services is referred to as labor. 
 
• The** income earned** by labor resources is called **wages** and is the largest source of income for most people.
 
 
 
• **Capital:**
 
 
• Consider capital as the **equipment, tools, and buildings **that people utilize to produce commodities and services.
 
• Depending on the worker and the sort of job being done, capital varies.
 
• **Interest **is the source of income for owners of capital resources.
 
 
 
• **Entrepreneurship:**
 
 
• An entrepreneur is a person who uses **capital, labor, and other production elements** in combination to turn a profit.
 
• **Profit **is how entrepreneurship gets compensated.

If 12 is subtracted from each of n values x₁, x₂, ⋯, xₙ, then the sum of the resulting numbers is 92. If 8 is subtracted from each of the n values, then the sum of the numbers is 208. What is the mean of the given n values?

(Give your answer correct to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If 12 is subtracted from each of n values x1, x2, ⋯, xn, then the sum of the resulting numbers is 92

If 8 is subtracted from each of the n values, then the sum of the numbers is 208

**Formula Used:**

Mean(Average) = Sum of observation/Number of observation.

**Calculation:**

Let the sum of n values** **x1, x2, x₃ ....., xₙ = X

n be the number of observations.

According to the question,

X - 12n = 92 (12 is substracted n times = 12n) ----(1)

X - 8n = 208 (8 is substracted n times = 8n) ----(2)

Subtract (1) from (2)

⇒ 4n = 116

n = 29

Put the value of n in (2)

X - (8 × 29) = 208

⇒ 208 + 232

⇒ 440

X = 440

Mean of the given n values = Sum of observation/Number of observation

⇒ X/29

⇒ 440/29

⇒ 15.172 ∼ 15.2

**∴ The mean of the given n values is 15.2.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest on Rs. 2,50,000 at 16% per annum for 9 months, compounded quarterly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **quarterly compounding**, the **Rate** becomes 16% ÷ 4 = 4% and **Time** becomes 9 ÷ 3 = 3 periods.

Use the **3 : 3 : 1 ratio method** for 3 periods at 4%:

Step 1: 4% of 2,50,000 = 10,000 | Step 2: 4% of 10,000 = 400 | Step 3: 4% of 400 = 16

**Compound Interest** = 3 × (10,000) + 3 × (400) + 1 × (16) = 30,000 + 1,200 + 16 = 31,216.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 31,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Principal (P)** = Rs. 2,50,000

⇒ **Annual Rate (R)** = 16%

⇒ **Time (T)** = 9 months

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Amount (A)** = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where r is the quarterly rate and n is the number of quarters.

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b84660cb2ed51463fe84a9e71f98cb7bc2c3fab921ce2e62fad79d22ffd96694.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 16% ÷ 4 = 4%

⇒ Number of quarters (n) = 9 months ÷ 3 months = 3 quarters

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × (1 + 4/100)³

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × (1.04)³

⇒ A = 2,50,000 × 1.124864

⇒ A = 281,216

⇒ CI = 281,216 − 2,50,000

⇒ CI = 31,216

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 31,216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded quarterly, divide the annual rate by 4 and multiply the time in years by 4. Formula: A = P(1 + R/400)⁴ⁿ.

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, divide the annual rate by 2 and multiply the time in years by 2. Formula: A = P(1 + R/200)²ⁿ.

Effective Interest Rate

It represents the actual interest earned in a year due to compounding. Effective Rate = (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where r is the nominal rate and n is the frequency.

CI − SI Difference for 3 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years is given by: D = P(r/100)² × (3 + r/100).</p

questions.question: The downhill movement of rock and soil under the direct influence of gravity is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass wasting.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass wasting** is the enormous **downward movement **of rock, soil, and debris caused by gravity. Mass wasting includes events like **debris flows, slumps, and rock falls.**
 
• **Rocks fall:**
 
 
• Rock falls happen when chunks of rock fall down a cliff. Large bricks may eventually get** loosened** as a result of **frost wedging, falling.**
 
• **Talus** is the term for the buildup of **rock fragments** at the bottom of a steep slope.
 
 
 
• **Slump:**
 
 
• The term "slump" refers to the** rotating slip of a large amount of bed rock** off a high cliff. The most frequent cause of slumping is** erosion at the slope's base,** which lessens the support provided for underlying sediments.
 
 
 
• **Debris avalanche:**
 
 
• The debris avalanche is the worst kind of debris flow. It flows **down steep slopes** in a quickly churning mass of dirt, water, rock debris, and air. By serving as a cushion between the debris and the underlying surface, the trapped air may quicken the avalanche.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mass wasting also includes rockslides, landslides, mudflow, creep etc.
 
 
• Rockslides: Typically, a **zone of weakness** is followed by a rockslide. **Slippage **is exacerbated by water presence. Rockslides typically originate from **collisions** down the **slope **shattering the boulder mass into debris.
 
• Landslides: **Large rocks** that break off and roll downhill cause landslides. Both really **heavy rain and earthquakes** frequently start it.
 
• Mudflow: A mudflow is a swiftly moving liquid mass made up of soil, rock fragments, and water. They are especially frequent in semiarid highland areas.
 
• Creep: Creep is the gradual and slow descent of soil. Usually, its velocity is less than one centimeter each year. The gradual movement of soil particles down the hill caused by freezing and thawing contributes to soil creep.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic action:**
 
 
• The** physical weathering and mechanical reaction **of earth elements to flowing water in rivers and streams, breaking waves, and storm surge along shorelines is referred to as hydraulic action.
 
 
 
• **Solifluction**:
 
 
• It a combination of **creep and flow**, creates distinct sheets, terraces, and lobes of rock and debris.
 
• On **steeper slopes **where the process has pushed **loosening boulders and dirt** downslope, solifluction sheets and lobes can be seen.

questions.question: A train 225 m long is running at a speed of 145 km/hr. What is the time (in seconds) in which it will pass a man who starts from the engine running at the speed of 17 km/hr in the direction opposite to that of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 145 + 17 = 162 km/hr.

Convert to m/s: 162 × (5/18) = 45 m/s.

Time = **Train Length** ÷ **Relative Speed** = 225 ÷ 45 = 5 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **Train** = 225 m

Speed of the **Train** (VT) = 145 km/hr

Speed of the **Man** (VM) = 17 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = V₁ + V₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b489440eea5c7d5a05c9d176dbbdb5932a469530516759aecba644bed41d90c6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 145 + 17 = 162 km/hr

⇒ To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18

⇒ Relative Speed = 162 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 9 × 5 = 45 m/s

⇒ Time taken to pass = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 225 ÷ 45

⇒ Time = 5 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 5 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = |V₁ − V₂|. When moving in **opposite directions**, relative speed = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a stationary man or pole, the **distance** covered is the length of the train itself. If crossing a platform, distance = Length of Train + Length of Platform.</p

BODMAS Rule

It ensures a standard sequence for solving mathematical expressions: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, then Addition/Subtraction.

Priority of Operations

Multiplication and Division have the same rank and should be solved from left to right as they appear in the expression.

Addition and Subtraction

questions.question: A goods train overtakes two boys who are walking in the same direction in which the train is going, at a rate of 5 kmph and 10 kmph and passes them completely in 21 and 24 seconds respectively. What is the length of the goods train (in metres)?

km/h × 5/18 = m/sec

When two bodies move in the same direction, then Relative speed = the Difference in their speeds

Speed of the second person in m/sec = 10 × 5/18 = 25/9 m/sec

So,

Again,

Relative speed of the train and the second person = {V – (25/9)}m/sec

⇒ V = L/24 + 25/9 ----(2)

⇒ (8L – 7L)/(168) = (50 – 25)/(18)

⇒ (L)/168 = 25/18 

⇒ L = (25/18) × 168

⇒ L = 233(1)/(3) m

**∴ The length of the train is 233(1)/(3) m.**
